Here is the persistence slice I committed, verbatim from `.gestalt/architecture/data.json` (with the one place `.gestalt/architecture/reconciled.json` supersedes it flagged explicitly).

## Conceptual tables

**`notifications` — EXTENDED (the only schema change)**
- Columns: `id`, `recipient_id`, `type`, `title`, `message`, `related_entity_type`, `related_entity_id`, **`related_entity_code` (NEW, nullable)**, `status`, `created_at`, `read_at`.
- PK: `id`. FK: `recipient_id -> employees.id`.
- Indexes: `id` (PK — the `findById` lookup and the `updateStatus` target); `(recipient_id, status)` (the approver's inbox read pattern, existing from the initial migration); `(related_entity_type, related_entity_id)` (correlates a notification with the leave request it concerns — specified in the GP-008 section of docs/ARCHITECTURE.md but ABSENT from the initial migration, reconciled in this feature's migration); `related_entity_code` deliberately NOT indexed (only ever read as part of a row already located by id or recipient).
- Why the new column: the approver notice must carry the leave type so the approver can act without a second lookup; without it the leave type is only reachable by joining back to `leave_requests`. The column is generic (a code for whatever `related_entity_type` names), not leave-specific, so the single notifications table stays one concept.

**`leave_requests` — UNCHANGED (referenced by name)**
- Columns: `id`, `employee_id`, `leave_type_code`, `start_date`, `end_date`, `requested_days`, `reason`, `status`, `approver_id`, `approval_comment`, `submitted_at`, `decided_at`, `cancelled_by`, `cancelled_at`, `reverses_request_id`.
- PK: `id`. FKs: `employee_id -> employees.id`; `leave_type_code -> leave_types.code`; `approver_id -> employees.id`; `cancelled_by -> employees.id`; `reverses_request_id -> leave_requests.id`.
- Indexes: `id` (PK — every cancel and single-read starts here); `(employee_id, status)` (existing composite; serves role-scoped list queries and owner/status guards, but NOT the pending-decisions query, which has no `employee_id` predicate); **`status` standalone (NEW)** — the pending-decisions filter; the existing `(employee_id, status)` cannot serve a status-only predicate as a leading column, and this feature's queue query is the first status-only access path in the codebase; **`approver_id` (NEW)** — recipient resolution for a cancelled APPROVED request and the APPROVED-inclusion variant of the queue (an FK with no supporting index today); `(leave_type_code, start_date)` (type filter, inclusive date-range filter, ORDER BY start_date DESC); `reverses_request_id` (UNIQUE, nullable — the GP-008 linkage and the DB backstop for exactly-once balance release; a cancelled-after-approval request is TWO rows, so any pending-decisions query MUST exclude rows whose `reverses_request_id` is non-null); `employee_id` (FK lookups and per-employee history).

**`employees` — UNCHANGED (referenced by name)**
- Columns: `id`, `employee_number`, `first_name`, `last_name`, `email`, `password_hash`, `role`, `manager_id`, `department`, `hire_date`, `termination_date`, `employment_status`.
- PK: `id`. FK: `manager_id -> employees.id`.
- Indexes: `id` (PK — FK target for `leave_requests.employee_id/approver_id/cancelled_by` and `notifications.recipient_id`); `manager_id` (the direct-report lookup; this feature reads it in the opposite direction — resolving a requester's direct manager for a SUBMITTED cancellation via `getEmployeeById(requesterId).managerId` — and it also scopes the MANAGER queue predicate); `email` (unique, login); `employee_number` (unique, natural key).

`audit_logs` and `leave_balances` are unchanged and are listed only as participants in the cancellation unit of work.

## Repository interfaces and concrete implementations

All five are backed by PostgreSQL via the shared `pg` Pool exported from `src/shared/db/connection.ts` (constructor-injected `dbPool: Pool = defaultPool`). Every method takes an optional trailing `PoolClient` and falls back to the shared pool via the private `db(client)` accessor; **no repository opens BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK**.

**`ILeaveRepository` → `PgLeaveRequestRepository`** (declared inline in `src/modules/leave/leave.repository.ts` — the balance convention, not a separate `.interface.ts` — re-exported from `src/modules/leave/index.ts`):
- `create(input: CreateLeaveRequestInput, client?: PoolClient): Promise<LeaveRequest>` — EXISTING, unchanged. Inserts all 15 columns including `reverses_request_id`; used for the GP-008 CANCELLED reversal row.
- `findById(id: string, client?: PoolClient): Promise<LeaveRequest | null>` — EXISTING, unchanged. Returns null when absent; the service decides error semantics.
- `findByReversesRequestId(reversesRequestId: string, client?: PoolClient): Promise<LeaveRequest | null>` — EXISTING, unchanged. The double-cancel guard for an APPROVED request.
- `update(id: string, changes: UpdateLeaveRequestDto, client?: PoolClient): Promise<LeaveRequest>` — EXISTING, unchanged. Dynamic SET from FIELD_COLUMNS; used ONLY for the in-place DRAFT/SUBMITTED cancellation. MUST NOT be called with the id of an APPROVED row (GP-008).
- `findByQuery(params: LeaveRequestQueryParams, client?: PoolClient): Promise<LeaveRequest[]>` — EXISTING, unchanged. Status/leaveTypeCode/date-range/employeeIds filters plus limit/offset, ORDER BY start_date DESC.
- `findPendingDecisions(...)` — **NEW**. ⚠️ Signature reconciled: `data.json` records `findPendingDecisions(approverId: string, client?: PoolClient): Promise<LeaveRequest[]>`; `reconciled.json` supersedes it with `findPendingDecisions(actorId: string, actorRole: EmployeeRole, client?: PoolClient): Promise<LeaveRequest[]>` (the role parameter is required to express the ADMIN/MANAGER/EMPLOYEE scoping). Semantics: `status = SUBMITTED` (bound from `LeaveStatus.SUBMITTED`, never a bare string) AND `reverses_request_id IS NULL`, scoped by role — ADMIN: no further predicate; MANAGER: the requester's `employees.manager_id = actorId`; EMPLOYEE: no rows. ORDER BY `start_date ASC, id ASC`. Read-only: no `forUpdate`, opens no transaction, returns an array (possibly empty), never null, never throws on no rows. CANCELLED is excluded by construction, which is what makes a cancelled request stop being listed.

**`INotificationRepository` → `PgNotificationRepository`** (declared in `src/modules/notification/notification.repository.interface.ts`, implemented in `notification.repository.ts`, both re-exported from `src/modules/notification/index.ts`):
- `create(input: CreateNotificationInput, client?: PoolClient): Promise<Notification>` — EXISTING, EXTENDED. Generates id via `randomUUID()`, stamps `createdAt`, defaults `status` to PENDING, `read_at` null. The INSERT column list, the `COLUMNS` constant, `NotificationRow` and `mapRow` all gain `related_entity_code`. The optional `client` is forwarded so the insert joins the caller's transaction — the mechanism by which a failed notification insert rolls back the cancellation.
- `findById(id: string, client?: PoolClient): Promise<Notification | null>` — EXISTING, unchanged.
- `updateStatus(id: string, status: NotificationStatus, readAt: Date | null, client?: PoolClient): Promise<Notification | null>` — EXISTING, unchanged.

**`IAuditRepository` → `PgAuditLogRepository`** (`audit.repository.interface.ts` / `audit.repository.ts`, re-exported from `src/modules/audit/index.ts`):
- `create(input: CreateAuditLogInput, client?: PoolClient): Promise<AuditLog>` — EXISTING, unchanged. Generates id via `randomUUID()`, stamps `occurredAt`, JSON-stringifies before/afterState. The optional client is forwarded so the CANCEL entry joins the cancellation's unit of work. The existing audit entry for a cancellation is NOT changed: one `AuditAction.CANCEL` record, `entityType` = LEAVE_REQUEST_ENTITY_TYPE, `entityId` = the ORIGINAL request id, beforeState = the request, afterState = the cancelled row (or the reversal row on the GP-008 path).
- `findById(id: string, client?: PoolClient): Promise<AuditLog | null>` — EXISTING, unchanged.
- `findByEntity(entityType: string, entityId: string): Promise<AuditLog[]>` — EXISTING, unchanged. Takes NO PoolClient: the read path opens no transaction and joins none.

**`IBalanceRepository` → `PgLeaveBalanceRepository`** (interfaces declared alongside the implementation in `src/modules/balance/balance.repository.ts`, re-exported from `src/modules/balance/index.ts`):
- `findByKey(employeeId: string, leaveTypeCode: LeaveTypeCode, periodStart: Date, periodEnd: Date, client?: PoolClient, forUpdate?: boolean): Promise<LeaveBalance | null>` — EXISTING, unchanged. The cancellation passes `forUpdate = true` so the row is locked before the release write; this is the lock that makes the release and the notification one atomic decision.
- `update(id: string, changes: Partial<LeaveBalance>, client?: PoolClient): Promise<LeaveBalance>` — EXISTING, unchanged. The single write that releases `requestedDays`: `pendingDays -= requestedDays` for a SUBMITTED cancellation, `usedDays -= requestedDays` for an APPROVED (GP-008 reversal) cancellation. Full release, no pro-rating.
- `findById(id: string, client?: PoolClient): Promise<LeaveBalance | null>` — EXISTING, unchanged.
- `create(input: CreateLeaveBalanceInput, client?: PoolClient): Promise<LeaveBalance>` — EXISTING, unchanged.

**`IEmployeeRepository` → `PgEmployeeRepository`** (`employee.repository.interface.ts` / `employee.repository.ts`, re-exported from `src/modules/employee/index.ts`):
- `findById(id: string, client?: PoolClient): Promise<Employee | null>` — EXISTING, unchanged. The recipient-resolution read: for a SUBMITTED cancellation the service loads the requester and takes `managerId` as the approver to notify.
- `findByManagerId(managerId: string, client?: PoolClient): Promise<Employee[]>` — EXISTING, unchanged. Not used by this feature's recipient resolution, but it is the reverse direction of the same relationship and the reason `manager_id` is indexed.
- `create(input: CreateEmployeeInput, client?: PoolClient): Promise<Employee>` — EXISTING, unchanged.
- `findByEmployeeNumber(employeeNumber: string, client?: PoolClient): Promise<Employee | null>` — EXISTING, unchanged.
- `findByEmail(email: string, client?: PoolClient): Promise<Employee | null>` — EXISTING, unchanged.

## Net change
One new repository method (`ILeaveRepository.findPendingDecisions`), one end-to-end extension (`INotificationRepository.create` for `related_entity_code`), one new column (`notifications.related_entity_code`), two new indexes (`leave_requests.status`, `leave_requests.approver_id`) plus the reconciled `(related_entity_type, related_entity_id)` index on `notifications`. No new table, no new module, no new dependency edge. `IAuditRepository`, `IBalanceRepository` and `IEmployeeRepository` are unchanged; their contracts are recorded because they participate in the cancellation unit of work or in recipient resolution.
